original_test_intent: Exercise the approved BIOS flash path for a bounded number of repeated iterations and prove every flash, activation and post-boot firmware/platform state remains correct without accumulating errors.
original_method: Obtain the exact BMC-provided command, compatible image, direction, count and timing; preserve the baseline; execute only the bounded approved loop with stable power and an activation checkpoint after each write; compare firmware, boot, health and logs per iteration and restore the approved final state.
manual_activity: The firmware/BMC owner supplies and approves the exact command, image, iteration count, direction, timing, per-iteration oracle and final state; an operator supervises power, activation and recovery readiness.
required_inputs: Exact board/SUT identity and complete current BIOS/ME/security/configuration state
BMC-provided flash command and supported AMI/EFI environment
Compatible signed image(s), hash/provenance and upgrade/downgrade/reflash sequence
Hard iteration count, activation timing and expected version/state at each iteration
Per-iteration pass/fail/abort matrix and approved final firmware/configuration state
Stable UPS/AC, protected console/OOB access and independently usable recovery image/process
safety_requirements: Reject execution while command, count, image, direction, timing, criteria or recovery remains TBD
Archive complete baseline before any clear and preserve raw evidence separately for every iteration
Enforce the approved hard count; never infer an extra cycle or loop until failure
Never interrupt a write or begin the next iteration before the prior boot and health gate passes
Stop on any flash, activation, version, ME/TPM, boot, device, event or count anomaly
Do not automatically retry or substitute a neighboring same-code method
Invoke only the approved recovery path and return the SUT to the authorized final state
agent_execution_scope: Validate all supplied loop parameters, target/image/tool identity and approval
Stage but do not execute the exact BMC command until every TBD field is closed
Collect pre-loop state and enforce count plus per-iteration transition gates
Retain raw flash status, boot lifecycle, version and platform-health evidence for each iteration
Abort before the next write on any mismatch and preserve recovery evidence
Report the full iteration matrix without issuing the final verdict
engineer_actions: Define and approve the command, image sequence, count, timing, criteria and final state
Confirm repeated-write necessity, stable power and recovery readiness
Adjudicate any failure before an additional write or recovery
Review cumulative and per-iteration evidence and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: DeepSeek correctly declines to invent a loop, but an AMI image and generic flash/reboot outline are insufficient without the BMC command, bounded sequence and per-iteration state oracle.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Do not execute a placeholder. After owner approval, run only the exact supplied BMC/AMI command for the exact hard-limited image sequence, with one validated flash/activation/health checkpoint per iteration and no automatic retry.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The multi-time intent, BMC-command dependency, TBD count/Criteria, private script and 20/2000-minute estimates remain explicit.

modernized_recommendation.status: BMC COMMAND, BOUNDED LOOP AND ACCEPTANCE MATRIX REQUIRED
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Convert the approved command and image sequence into a finite state machine whose next write is permitted only after raw flash success, activation, identity and platform-health checks from the current iteration.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Supplies the missing hard limit, per-iteration gate, abort/recovery and final-state contract without inventing their values.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A final BIOS string cannot reveal an intermediate failed write, skipped activation, accumulated event fault or wrong number of completed iterations.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Repeated writes multiply power-loss and region-coherency exposure; endurance implications and any flash-cycle limit remain owner/vendor decisions.

project_override_considerations: The Project must provide the missing command/count/criteria and may choose a vendor-supported reduced sequence, but must not borrow the row-690 SMBIOS or row-1562 AC-loss method merely because the code is duplicated.
expected_evidence: Variant identity, approved BMC command/tool/image sequence, hashes, direction, count, timing and final-state matrix
Per-iteration raw command/output/exit status and uninterrupted-write evidence
Per-iteration activation/boot milestones, exact versions and ME/TPM/device/health/log comparison
Hard-count audit, abort/recovery record where applicable and restored approved final state
Engineer-owned PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source is incomplete rather than internally contradictory: it explicitly leaves command, test count and Criteria TBD. Those fields must be supplied as readiness inputs and cannot be inferred.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The missing command, bounded count, image sequence and criteria are finite owner/BMC inputs. Until supplied execution is prohibited, but the testcase is conditionally automatable rather than permanently blocked.

review_improvement: Retains DeepSeek's refusal to invent the loop while adding a hard count, per-iteration state machine, cumulative evidence, abort and final-state recovery contract.
independent_technical_reasoning: A repeated-flash case is not equivalent to running a single flash command in a shell loop. Each completed write changes the starting state and risk for the next one, so authorization must advance only after an iteration-specific activation and health checkpoint.
